business_rules.statement: For every capability the platform grants, the catalog carries an explicit-denial test. A permission matrix that has only been tested in the affirmative has not been tested.
The traceability conformance check runs and must pass before anything else executes; an orphan holds the release with no promotion.
Any capability with pending or failing scenarios cannot be enabled, and the build cannot be promoted with such a capability marked enabled.
business_rules.applies_to: atoms, agents, composed agents, retrieval, on-device deterministic layer

business_rules.statement: The evaluation gate has no off position for any account; neither a Platform Engineer, nor an Admin, nor the Root Super Admin can proceed past it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin platform console / platform runtime

business_rules.statement: The on-device severity-classification table is a versioned artifact with scenario coverage, re-evaluated at every version before it distributes.
There is no control anywhere on the Eval Harness screen that disables the gate, weakens a scenario's verdict, or marks a failing scenario as accepted, because none exists in the platform.
Every test in Sections 50.5 through 50.19 carries exactly nine mandatory fields; a record missing any field is rejected before execution.

The Command Center action set is closed at ten, and four things are deliberately impossible for every role: overriding a specification or evaluation gate, pausing or stopping a run, editing any record or configuration, and creating Jobs or runs.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Client Command Center, application programming interface

business_rules.statement: The same rule must be enforced at four independent enforcement points — user interface, application programming interface, background jobs, and synchronization. Any divergence is a defect, whether a wrongful allow or a wrongful denial.
Every attempt, allowed or denied, must be present in the audit log, and the change and its audit event must have committed in the same transaction.
AVIIXA holds nine human security role types across two separate security domains: four platform console role types and five tenant role types.
Scopes are Tenant, Site, and Area, held simultaneously and orthogonally; multi-role is additive; the audit log records identity and action, never acting-as-role.
A refusal does not disclose whether the identifier exists; a response distinguishing not-found from not-permitted leaks existence across the tenant boundary.
business_rules.enforcement_point: application programming interface and user interface

business_rules.statement: Cross-tenant analytics anonymisation is one of the six ENFORCED invariants and has no off position for any account including the root.
A finished run does not accept a fold-in capture; late data after finish follows the audited-recompute rule instead. An archived Job accepts no execution.
There is no act-on-behalf-of capability anywhere on the platform; delegation exists only as the four named grants.
Segregation of duties is absolute regardless of how many roles one identity holds; no role performs two stages on one submission and the Release Authority cannot be bypassed.
business_rules.applies_to: Author, Reviewer, Release Authority; Job creator

business_rules.statement: Every approval-chain transition is permanently recorded with role, timestamp, version, and comments; a published version whose approval record shows fewer than three distinct transitions is a defect.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate; the specification gate and the evaluation gate are hard, always, for every tenant, and cannot be set to either posture.
A qualification-expiry warning schedule later than the defaults is rejected at the point of entry with the bound stated; an earlier schedule is accepted.
business_rules.enforcement_point: point of entry, platform floor register

business_rules.statement: The compliance-emergency path is the only write route into tenant data and requires two authorisations, with scope declared before it opens; ambient browsing exists nowhere on the console.
business_rules.applies_to: Root Super Admin plus one Admin

business_rules.statement: Cached credentials are trusted only within a bounded window; past it the device does not extend trust. On reconnection a change is delivered, validated, applied, acknowledged, and reconciled, in that order and visibly.

Administration and telemetry expose metadata, counts, rates, and statuses only, never operational content. Record-level operational content is reachable only through one of the three named, audited, session-scoped access classes.
A schedule definition is an authored object under the same authority rules as the thing it triggers; where the action is critical class the schedule definition is critical class too.
Every occurrence is bound to exactly one tenant and revalidates that binding at execution.
Any revalidation failure denies the occurrence, records the denial with its specific cause, and does not retry the denied condition blindly.
An occurrence that cannot be audited does not happen — the occurrence result and its audit event commit together.
Calendar triggers are evaluated in the Site's timezone, never in a server timezone and never in coordinated universal time alone.

A calendar trigger whose civil time occurs twice — the daylight-saving-time repeated hour — must fire exactly once. Firing twice is a duplicate official effect and is forbidden by the idempotency rule.

Device clock drift never decides anything on its own; server-receipt time is authoritative for ordering at sync and skew beyond the tenant threshold is flagged as an operational event with consequences, not merely logged.

A skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed; the record carries the unflagged version until a Quality Manager resolves the conflict individually, and skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All.
At-least-once triggering must produce idempotent official effects; the occurrence identifier is the idempotency key.
Trigger firing or queueing is never reported as completed business work; a schedule list showing ran at 06:00 when the occurrence is still executing is a defect.

Claiming uses a lease with a fencing token so that a slow replica's late write is rejected; the superseding replica's write stands and the fenced replica records supersession, not failure, and performs no compensating action.

Paused, cancelled, expired, or superseded schedules cannot execute at all, and their non-execution is recorded; a claimed occurrence for a paused definition must be denied at revalidation, not completed because it was already in flight.

A cancelled definition remains in the list, greyed, with its cancellation recorded — it is not removed, because removal would erase the evidence that it existed. A cancelled definition cannot be resumed; a new definition must be created.
The Client Command Center shows a command as applied only on device acknowledgement, never on creation or delivery.

The deterministic on-device layer is unaffected by any server-side infrastructure failure; gates, specification checks, severity classification, and the Severity 1 hold run on the device using the version-pinned work package.
Nothing is purged, so no failure or recovery path may delete; the resolution of an inconsistency is an append-only correction.
Media is evicted from the device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on the strength of an attempted upload.
Captured media stays in the application's encrypted store and never touches the device gallery.
Storage-full behaviour is explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification and no behaviour may be invented here.

A run cannot start on a package that cannot classify: a corrupt package and a package missing severity mappings both refuse to start; a package missing a coaching asset starts and falls back to the step's authored Work Instructions.
An in-flight run is never rebased; it finishes on the version it started on, and the version change takes effect at the next execution boundary with the mandatory republish description shown.

A conflict whose two values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits is passed to the rule-based deviation mechanism as a quality event; no artificial-intelligence model participates in the classification.

No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device using the limits and severity mappings carried in the version-pinned work package; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.
Nothing an agent proposes reaches a worker or changes a record without a human gate or pre-authorised policy, and the platform never invents content, rules, or thresholds.
Tenants compose reasoning agents only; tenant-composed action agents are deferred.

Emergency pause renders as agent unavailability, never as silence; in-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park, raised gates stay human-decidable, resume is a separate audited act, and it never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
A partial artificial-intelligence output never becomes official; it is discarded or marked incomplete, and nothing partial enters the record.
Ingested content is treated as data, never as instruction; prohibited actions are structurally unavailable to the agent rather than merely discouraged.

Seven fallback prohibitions bound every fallback: no bypass of role-based access control, no cross-tenant reach, no bypass of qualification, specifications, evaluation, approval, publication, or Severity 1 hold and release rules; no silent discard or overwrite; no stale-as-current or failure-as-success; no indefinite dependence on one person; no infinite retry loop.
For compliance suspension the worker-facing message is exactly: Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.
Where no holder of the target role is on shift, the platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery.
Nothing is machine-translated at runtime, anywhere; a locale-completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale.
The audit log is append-only, immutable, complete, with no delete or edit path on any surface, and is never shorter-lived than the tenant data it evidences.
business_rules.enforcement_point: all surfaces and the application programming interface

business_rules.statement: Cross-tenant access events mirror into the affected tenant's own stream; the tenant-facing Platform Access History reads the same records rather than a separate summary. One audit truth per tenant.
business_rules.applies_to: support sessions and JBS access grants

business_rules.statement: A tenant override cannot defeat a global disable; tenants may be stricter, never looser than the platform floor, and the platform rejects rather than logs.
An unknown feature fails closed — unavailable rather than available — when the feature-control store is unreachable; no platform-fixed guarantee depends on the feature-control store at all.
The console reports a feature change as propagating with the count of nodes not yet carrying it, never as applied everywhere.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact; the local store is preserved, not wiped.

The canonical names and codes of the eight starter Job Types and eight starter Service Type tags must never be invented; where the client has supplied no name the seeded catalogue holds no entry at all.

Service Type is optional metadata on which no platform behaviour hangs; pre-population of qualification requirements is a creation-time convenience default only and the tag never decides. Release Authority is explicitly not assigned per Service Type.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub, Standards and Operations Studio

business_rules.statement: A referenced taxonomy entry cannot be destructively deleted; deprecation is the available path and historical resolution is preserved.
business_rules.applies_to: Job Types and Service Type tags

business_rules.statement: The platform floor register rejects rather than logs: a looser-than-floor value fails at the point of entry with the bound stated, and the platform never accepts an out-of-bound configuration and remembers it apologetically.
Severity 1 actions can be added, never removed; genealogy depth cannot be reduced below one level plus rework history.
An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, and an action that cannot be audited does not happen.

A tenant may configure a Command Center refresh faster than the default only if the deployment's scale supports it; the validation runs before the interval applies and can refuse with the reason stated.
A regression against the previous release's performance baseline is raised as a defect even where no absolute target exists.
A platform-fixed guarantee breach at layer four blocks release irrespective of the probability of the failure combination, and is never closed on the grounds that it did not recur.
Claiming complete coverage while any open decision remains is prohibited.
A release held is an acceptable outcome; a release accepted on unknown coverage is not.
No test may create, alter, or delete data in a production tenant. Test data is synthetic or drawn from a non-production tenant.
An acceptance report is never overwritten; an amendment is an addition and the original remains readable, and a superseded acceptance criterion remains readable in the release that accepted it.

decisions.question: An enabled capability whose evaluations begin failing is flagged immediately; does it stop?
options: stopped at the moment of flagging
decisions.impact: Determines whether unevaluated behaviour may keep running on a factory floor.

decisions.question: Is the sync-conflict panel never a blocker, or does a skew-flagged record constitute a per-record block until a Quality Manager resolves it?
options: per-record block on the skewed value (§6.11.3)
decisions.impact: Determines whether floor work can proceed while a skew-flagged conflict awaits review.

decisions.question: How are server-receipt-time ordering (§7.10.4) and last-write-wins by device timestamp (§7.10.8) reconciled?
decisions.impact: Determines which timestamp decides a conflict outcome on the quality record.

decisions.question: Who is the acceptance authority for a release? Not named anywhere in the Statement of Work.
decisions.impact: Nobody is named to sign the acceptance report or accept exceptions.

decisions.question: How does delivery test-suite ownership transition from JBS to the client's platform team at handover?
decisions.impact: No handover date or transition procedure for test-suite ownership exists.

decisions.question: What is the drift canary's cadence value?
decisions.impact: Sets how often enabled capabilities are re-verified against their scenarios.

decisions.question: What does the device do at the moment the offline credential-trust window lapses mid-run — lock, park, or continue read-only?
decisions.impact: Determines worker behaviour at the trust-window boundary while still offline.

decisions.question: What is the scheduler replica clock-drift alerting threshold?
decisions.impact: Sets when replica drift is raised as an operational alert.

decisions.question: What is the artificial-intelligence confidence threshold and where is it set?
options: per-tenant thresholds within a platform floor
decisions.impact: Too high suppresses guidance; too low presents guesses to a factory floor.

decisions.question: How much prompt-injection input validation should be implemented, and at what cost?
options: layered defence per OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
decisions.impact: Determines residual nuisance-manipulation risk versus latency and engineering cost.

decisions.question: Which accessibility standard and level does the platform commit to, and which chapter owns it?
options: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2 level AA for the four web surfaces plus corresponding mobile guidance for the Frontline Worker Application
decisions.impact: Accessibility is procurement-relevant and no blueprint chapter currently owns it.

decisions.question: What are the performance and capacity targets and any service-level agreement?
decisions.impact: No contractual response-time, throughput, session, device, or storage limit exists.

decisions.question: What is the Recovery Time Objective for the testing and acceptance function?
decisions.impact: A long testing outage delays every release; tolerable delay is a commercial decision.

decisions.question: Which schedule-definition edit classes re-enter approval?
decisions.impact: Determines whether an edited schedule may execute under new terms without approval.

decisions.question: What disposition applies to a calendar trigger whose civil time falls in the daylight-saving-time gap?
options: fire at the first valid instant after the gap
fire at the instant the gap began in the prior offset
decisions.impact: A skipped compliance-relevant occurrence and a shifted one have different consequences.

decisions.question: What disposition applies to a monthly calendar trigger on a day that does not exist in a given month?
options: roll to the first of the next month
decisions.impact: A monthly compliance report that silently skips February is a gap in a tenant's evidence.

decisions.question: What is the bounded backfill bound for missed occurrences?
options: a fixed number of missed occurrences per definition
decisions.impact: An unbounded backfill after a long regional outage is itself an outage.

decisions.question: What are the timeout and retry values for a scheduled occurrence?
options: per-definition values within a platform ceiling
decisions.impact: Too short causes spurious retries; too long hides a stuck system.

decisions.question: What is the default overlap posture for a schedule?
decisions.impact: The wrong default silently changes behaviour for every schedule that does not declare.

decisions.question: What are the per-tenant concurrency limits for scheduled work?
decisions.impact: Prevents one tenant's backlog delaying another tenant's schedule.

decisions.question: On resume of a paused schedule, do missed occurrences backfill or are they skipped?
decisions.impact: Determines disposition of occurrences missed during a pause.

decisions.question: On reconnection, do commands apply before captures upload, or do captures upload first?
decisions.adopted_working_position: stop-class commands apply before captures upload, then the full capture queue drains, then enabling-class commands apply last
decisions.impact: Determines whether a suspension can land before evidence is lost or after a backlog drains.

decisions.question: Is the Prevention Agent gated at authoring time by pre-authorised policy, or by a runtime human gate for every effect?
options: runtime human gate for every action agent (§8.3.2, §8.3.3)
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field: authoring-time policy for the Prevention Agent, runtime human gate for the Deviation and Containment Agent's proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, none — reasoning agent for every reasoning agent
decisions.impact: Determines how much human oversight actually exists on the floor.

decisions.question: What releases a soft suspension — an explicit operator signal or an automatic payment event?
options: explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console (§4.2.4)
decisions.adopted_working_position: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, taken by the client's platform team when it clears the commercial hold, with no payment event observed because there is no payment integration at V1
decisions.impact: Without it a tenant could stay suspended waiting for a payment event the platform cannot receive.

decisions.question: Which capture-type set is authoritative?
options: the §5.5.3 set of seven capture types
decisions.adopted_working_position: adopted on the §5.5.3 set — the adopted seven, dropdown selection and multi-item checkbox confirmation included
decisions.impact: Determines which capture types a run must support offline.

decisions.question: What are the canonical names and codes of the eight starter Job Types and eight starter Service Type tags?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the platform-seeded catalogue ships empty at version 1, every tenant creates its own Job Types and Service Type tags immediately at every tier, and the later load of the client-supplied sixteen affects no tenant-created entry
decisions.status: adopted working position; names still owed
decisions.impact: Taxonomy names embed in tenant reporting and are expensive to change afterwards.

decisions.question: Are the platform-seeded catalogs administrable by Super Admin at all?
decisions.impact: The Super Admin taxonomy screen is not designed until this lands.

decisions.question: What is the global taxonomy versioning, deprecation, replacement, and archival model?
decisions.impact: Conditions AC-PROOF-042 on referenced-taxonomy protection.

decisions.question: What are the regional-failover posture, Recovery Time Objective, Recovery Point Objective, backup and restore procedure, and platform clock-source requirement?
options: warm standby in a second region
decisions.impact: Determines the architecture, not merely the procedure; retrofitting a Recovery Point Objective is far more expensive.

decisions.question: Engineering capability enablement authority versus generic tenant feature-value authority: §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval; §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes Admin actions.
decisions.impact: Determines who may change a tenant's feature values.

decisions.question: What is the global feature-control approval authority?
decisions.impact: Determines who approves a platform-wide feature change.

decisions.question: Global disable versus tenant-specific override precedence — which direction counts as stricter for a given feature?
decisions.impact: Conditions AC-PROOF-029.

decisions.question: Tenant override versus tier entitlement precedence.
decisions.impact: Conditions AC-PROOF-029.

decisions.question: What happens to in-flight and version-pinned work when a feature is disabled?
decisions.impact: Determines the precise in-flight rule for a mid-run feature disable.

decisions.question: What is the last-known-good staleness bound for feature control during a provider outage?
decisions.impact: An unbounded stale window means a disable never lands on a partitioned node.

decisions.question: What is the command expiry duration for a queued command a device has not collected?
decisions.impact: A command with no expiry can land arbitrarily far in the future on a device left in a drawer.

decisions.question: Does an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch version without a second approval, or must it pass the three-stage chain?
options: three-stage chain with explicit human sign-off at each stage (§5.11.1)
auto-publish with no second approval and no ceremony (§5.16.3, §6.7.4)
decisions.impact: Determines whether a published change carries one or three approval transitions.

decisions.question: What ordering do the shorthand forms Supervisor+ and QM+ imply across five non-hierarchical roles?
decisions.impact: A test suite assuming a hierarchy would encode an assumption the source does not make.

decisions.question: What is the device storage-full behaviour?
decisions.status: open — explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification, per platform; no behaviour may be invented
decisions.impact: Only the invariants holding under every candidate behaviour can be asserted today.

decisions.question: What are the deprecation, disablement, rollback of a deployed composed agent, and the fate of its in-flight runs?
decisions.impact: Composed-agent lifecycle behaviour cannot be asserted, only recorded.

decisions.question: How does remote wipe behave against an offline device?
decisions.impact: Interacts with compliance suspension's promise that local evidence is preserved.

decisions.question: Does the work package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's level?
decisions.adopted_working_position: until resolved, the package definition carries all levels and TEST-VERCOMPAT-001 asserts that reading
decisions.impact: Determines package size and offline content availability.

decisions.question: What is the escalation default when no holder of the target role is on shift?
options: escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.impact: The night-shift Severity 1 escalation path is not settled.

decisions.question: Are the record-finish window's bounds open or settled?
options: settled at twenty-four hours to seven days in two others
decisions.adopted_working_position: TEST-INV-004 asserts the settled bounds of twenty-four hours to seven days and records the divergence
decisions.impact: Determines the enforceable bound on the record-finish window.

decisions.question: What is the ITAR and EAR posture? Unresolved-structural with nothing ITAR-flavoured committed.
decisions.impact: No ITAR-flavoured behaviour may be tested or claimed.

decisions.question: What is the standardised device profile / published minimum device specification?
decisions.adopted_working_position: until it lands, TEST-CAP-002 measures against the interim assumed specification and reports the measurement
decisions.impact: Pre-staging policy cannot be pass/fail tested without it.

decisions.question: What is the archived-data retrieval expectation?
decisions.impact: Referenced by the data-pipeline scheduled-work test.

decisions.question: Referenced unresolved in the corrupt-package and version-compatibility coverage row.
decisions.impact: Conditions the versioning and work-package families.

decisions.question: Referenced by this chapter without resolution.
decisions.impact: Listed among existing decisions referenced but not resolved.

contradictions.description: Source says an enabled capability whose evaluations start failing is flagged immediately; it does not say the capability is stopped.

contradictions.description: The conflict panel is stated as never a blocker, yet a skew-flagged record carries the unflagged version until a Quality Manager resolves it individually — a per-record block.
conflicting_values: §6.11.2 never a blocker; work never stops waiting on conflict review
§6.11.3 skew-flagged write cannot win unreviewed; individual Quality Manager resolution required

contradictions.description: Server-receipt time is authoritative for ordering at sync, while the conflict rule is last-write-wins by device timestamp; the source never states the reconciliation.
The three-stage approval chain requires explicit human sign-off at each of three stages, while Lane B auto-publish describes a patch version publishing with no second approval and no ceremony.
conflicting_values: §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 auto-publish with no second approval

contradictions.description: Prevention Agent gating: described as operating entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy with a runtime gate only for proposals beyond it, and separately labelled action, gated with every action agent routing through a human gate before any effect.

contradictions.description: Soft-suspension release: one reading has the platform acting on the operator's signal with no payment integration at V1; another gives the exit as automatic on payment.

§8.9.2 and Part IX automatic on payment

contradictions.description: Reconnection ordering: safety argues commands first because a suspension, wipe, or hold must land before more work; data integrity argues captures first because unsynced evidence must never be risked.

contradictions.description: Atom enablement is a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval, while platform-side tenant current-value changes are Admin actions.

controls.label: Resolve All
controls.effect: Accepts the most recent version of every listed ordinary conflict in one action; excludes skew-flagged entries.

controls.label: Request release with a note
controls.effect: Requests a lot release which only a Quality Manager may perform.

controls.label: End-session
controls.effect: Tenant terminates an in-progress support session from the tenant-visible banner.

controls.label: Pause
controls.effect: Pauses a schedule definition; requires the underlying action's authority and a reason.

controls.label: Resume
controls.effect: Resumes a paused schedule definition; a cancelled definition cannot be resumed.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.effect: Cancels a schedule definition; it stays greyed in the list, never removed.

controls.label: Manual trigger
controls.effect: Creates a new occurrence; requires the underlying authority and is audited.

controls.label: Replay
controls.effect: Re-executes a specific past occurrence idempotently against its original identifier.

controls.label: Backfill
controls.effect: Executes a bounded set of missed occurrences; must respect the backfill bound.

controls.label: Suite runner
controls.effect: Runs one scenario or a whole suite on demand; recorded as an audited eval run.

controls.label: Gate view
controls.effect: Blocking list naming the failing scenario that blocks each capability.

controls.label: Drift canary panel
controls.effect: Shows the cadence, the last run, the verdict, and the named owner.

controls.label: ENFORCED badge
controls.effect: Renders each of the six invariants locked with no control for any account.

controls.label: Emergency pause
controls.effect: Suspends agent activity platform-wide or per tenant; critical class, root approval.

controls.label: Resume (emergency)
controls.effect: Separate audited critical-class act with its own root approval.

controls.label: Manual sync control
controls.effect: Convenience only, never a dependency; sync resumes automatically on reconnection.

controls.label: Deprecate (rendered in place of delete when referenced)
controls.effect: Blocks new assignment while preserving historical resolution; shows the reference count.

controls.label: Class-filtered export
controls.effect: Exports the audit set for external retention; no edit control exists.
